newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees long-term GNP at 7.5-8.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees long-term GNP at 7.5-8.5 pct.

text.p: The Philippines is projected to sustain a gross national product (GNP) growth rate of 7.5 to 8.5 percent from 1998 to the year 2000, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said in his report to the Cabinet on Tuesday.
In terms of gross domestic product (GDP), which excludes income from abroad, growth is forecast to run up to a yearly 8.3 percent from 1998 to the year 2000.

From 1998 onwards, the government expects to end its status as a borrowing country in the International Monetary Fund upon the completion of the three-year Extended Fund Facility which is due to finish in mid-1997, Ocampo said.
For 1997, the government is aiming for a GNP growth of seven to eight percent.
De Ocampo, who attended the IMF-World Bank meetings last month, reported to the Cabinet the results of the meetings with the IMF.
The country's economic pefromance would be further fortified if the government succeeds in completing the economic reforms it has set out to undertake, De Ocampo said.

He listed the following: the comprehensive tax reform programme, the streamlining of the public sector, the deregulation of the oil industry, restructuring of the electricity sector, further investment liberalization and the development of the capital markets.
